comment: D4 — key backup encryption vectors. Spec authority: identity/key-management.md §7 and ak.schema.key_backup.v1. These exercise the active v1 `passphrase_kdf` branch for `secret_storage` envelopes: the client derives the backup root key locally from an implementation-selected passphrase, encrypts before PUT /_arkret/self/keys/backups/{backup_id}, and the server stores only the opaque envelope. The standard user-facing recovery credential remains the 24-word Recovery Key; `mls_history` MUST use `recovery_public_key` or `secret_storage_key` and MUST NOT use `passphrase_kdf`. Restore re-derives the local key from signed metadata, verifies AEAD, and decrypts locally. Rotation creates a new backup_id or backup_version and uploads a freshly encrypted envelope before old retention expires.

vectors.name: client_side_passphrase_derives_master_key
vectors.comment: Client derives the recovery master key locally from a passphrase + random salt via Argon2id at memory_kib>=65536, iterations>=3, parallelism>=1. The plaintext passphrase NEVER leaves the client. Server sees only the derived encrypted blob.

expected.rationale: Client-side KDF: passphrase stays local; salt is uploaded with the blob so future restore can re-derive the same key.

vectors.name: server_side_blob_storage_opaque
vectors.comment: After client encrypts, the upload is ak.schema.key_backup.v1: {backup_id, actor_id, backup_kind, backup_version, encryption, contents, ciphertext, ciphertext_digest}. Server treats ciphertext as opaque bytes and persists by backup_id. Server cannot decrypt without the passphrase.

expected.rationale: Zero-knowledge backup: server stores ciphertext blob + KDF parameters; cannot derive plaintext without the user's passphrase.

vectors.name: restore_path_redrives_key_and_decrypts
vectors.comment: Client restores: GET /_arkret/self/keys/backups/{backup_id} -> re-derive master key from local passphrase + envelope salt + Argon2id params -> decrypt with XChaCha20-Poly1305 using envelope nonce/auth tag -> recover MLS history or secret-storage material. Successful decryption proves passphrase correctness and blob integrity.

expected.rationale: Restore re-derives the same master key (deterministic given passphrase+salt+iterations); AEAD verifies integrity AND correct passphrase atomically.

vectors.name: rotation_mints_new_version_and_reencrypts
vectors.comment: User rotates passphrase. Client derives a new master key with a new salt, re-encrypts all covered material, and uploads a new backup object/version. Server retains the old envelope until migration is confirmed or retention expires. Rotation must not silently drop covered material.

expected.rationale: Rotation is atomic re-encrypt + upload of every session key under the new master key; both versions coexist until migration confirmed.

negative_vectors.name: weak_argon2id_params_rejected
negative_vectors.comment: Client tries to upload with Argon2id memory_kib=32768, below the 65536 minimum. Server MUST refuse since this is a client misconfiguration that weakens the backup against offline brute-force.

expected.rationale: Backup blob Argon2id parameters MUST meet the default floor; below this the passphrase is too easily brute-forced.

negative_vectors.name: wrong_passphrase_aead_rejects
negative_vectors.comment: Restore client supplies wrong passphrase. Derived master key differs; AEAD auth_tag verification fails; client MUST refuse to use any partially-decrypted data.

expected.rationale: XChaCha20-Poly1305 auth tag fails for any wrong key; client MUST treat partial decryption as failure (no plaintext leak).
